free_tier.stated: A single metered rate of USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour, billed per second, with memory included and no tiers. Paused VMs, stopped VMs, commits, snapshots and branches do not accrue compute. No monthly minimum and no per-fork fee. 'New accounts get credits to prototype and run small experiments before a card is required' (amount not stated).

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: Paused VMs are free, so the shape that pays off is a fleet of branched computers parked between agent steps: 100 paused branches cost nothing, and only the one being worked on bills at USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour.
limits_note: No session cap, no idle reap and no monthly minimum are published; the first thing that actually stops a fleet is the monthly card charge for whatever ran, since paused VMs accrue nothing.
binding_note: No session cap, no idle reap and no monthly minimum are published; the first thing that actually stops a fleet is the monthly card charge for whatever ran, since paused VMs accrue nothing.

identity_cost.detail: The credit amount is not stated, and which identifier the account is created with is not stated in the evidence

evidence.proved: USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour, 1 second granularity, no per-branch fee, paused and stopped VMs do not accrue, 4 vCPUs 24x7 for a month is USD 116.80, and new accounts get credits before a card is required
CLI defaults are 2 vCPUs and 4096 MiB memory, so the default computer costs USD 0.08 per hour at the published rate

notes: The free credit amount is not published anywhere, so the free lane is recorded as unquantified rather than guessed. Storage for kept commits is billed and its rate is not on the pricing page. Isolation is a full VM rather than a microVM or container. For a month of 24/7 at the CLI default of 2 vCPU / 4 GiB the arithmetic is 2 x 730 x 0.04 = USD 58.40, which sits between bunny.net (USD 43.80 at 2 core / 4 GB) and inis.run (about USD 29.50 equivalent).
